title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Next.js / E2B / Vercel Platforms)
description:
We're hiring a senior full-stack engineer to help us launch MythOS Pro, an AI-powered operating system for local service businesses (barbershops, salons, restaurants). It's a full platform: CRM, booking/calendar, payments, inventory, a workforce module, an AI agent (Mylo) that runs across all of it, and a website builder. You'll work directly with the founder and grow into a core engineering role as we get launch-ready. Strong English communication required.

Priority #1 — Website Builder (the immediate need):

Our builder lets a customer import their GitHub repo, edit their Next.js site inside our platform, then push to main, which triggers an automatic Vercel redeploy so their live site updates. We need this pipeline rock-solid:



Fix reliability issues with our E2B sandbox (sandboxes sometimes fail to load / dev server doesn't bind correctly on port 3000). Reference: e2b-dev/fragments.

Build a clean GitHub repo import flow: clone repo into the sandbox (sandbox.git.clone), npm install, boot the Next.js dev server, expose the preview URL into our editor iframe.

Implement edit ? commit ? push-to-main back to the customer's GitHub repo via the GitHub App (installation token).

Wire the push to trigger Vercel auto-redeploy, with each customer's site served on their own subdomain via Vercel for Platforms (multi-tenant). Help us finish setting this up.

Sandbox lifecycle management: create, auto-pause on idle, resume on edit, kill on session end, with cost controls.



Beyond the builder, there's a deep backlog across the whole platform — CRM, booking, payments integrations, inventory, the workforce module, and Mylo's agent capabilities. We want someone who can own significant pieces of the product and help drive us to launch.

Our stack:



Frontend/API surface (mythOS-pro): Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Supabase, Tailwind, deployed on Vercel.

Agent runtime (mythos-claw): a custom Rust runtime that powers our Mylo agent — built on a fork of NEAR AI's IronClaw, blended with OpenClaw, Hermes, GoClaw, and other components. Runs as a long-running service on Google Cloud Run (Postgres/Neon, Redis/Upstash, embedded Hermes worker, Gemini integration).

Other: GitHub App integration, E2B sandboxes, Vercel for Platforms (multi-tenant), Claude API, Pinecone vector search.



The two runtimes communicate over HTTP — mythOS-pro is the public-facing surface, mythos-claw is the brain.

Must have: Deep Next.js App Router + TypeScript experience and the ability to debug deployment/infra issues independently (Cloud Run, Vercel, sandboxed dev environments). Strong bonus / what sets you apart: Rust experience and comfort working in an agent runtime — we'd love someone who can contribute to mythos-claw itself, not just the Next.js surface.

The show is hosted by Omar Khan, Founder of

Each episode is a focused deep-dive into one standout creative campaign or idea. The structure per episode is tight and punchy:

A fast, energetic intro

Campaign breakdown — what it is, why it works, what makes it clever

Regional relevance — what it means for UAE/Middle East audiences and brands

One full-length edited episode (5–10 minutes) optimised for YouTube

3–4 short-form social cuts optimised for Instagram Reels, TikTok, and LinkedIn

Captions/subtitles as standard throughout

Thumbnail asset for YouTube



The Editing Style

This is the most important section. Please read it carefully before applying.

We are looking for visually rich, creator-native editing. Think dynamic motion graphics, animated text overlays, sharp cuts, colour, and energy throughout. This is emphatically not B-roll with captions dropped on top. Every visual choice should serve the storytelling and amplify the host's energy.

title: Senior UGC Video Editor (Meta Ads) + B-Roll Sourcing + AI Generation
description:
We're a performance marketing agency running paid social for DTC brands across supplements, beauty, real estate, and lifestyle verticals. We spend serious money on Meta every month and creative is the lever that d
 whether accounts scale or stall. We're not looking for someone to just "cut videos" — we're looking for a creative partner who understands that on Meta, the editor is the media buyer's most important teammate.



We test creative aggressively. Winners get scaled, losers get killed, and we iterate weekly. The editors we love are the ones who treat every ad like a hypothesis and every variant like a data point.



THE ROLE



You'll own the post-production pipeline for multiple brands. That means taking raw UGC footage, creator deliverables, product shots, sourced B-roll, and AI-generated assets and turning them into ad variants that print money on Meta.



Three pillars to this role:



1. Editing. You can cut a UGC ad in your sleep — hooks, pacing, captions, sound design, the works.



2. Sourcing B-roll. A huge part of making UGC ads work is finding the right supporting footage. That means knowing where to pull stock clips, digging through Pinterest and TikTok for reference and inspiration, finding free-use clips on YouTube, scraping competitor ads fro
ta ad library, and knowing which clips are licensed for commercial use vs. which will get us in trouble. Half the battle is taste — knowing the exact shot that lands the message — and the other half is research speed.



3. Generating B-roll and A-roll with AI. When sourced footage doesn't exist or doesn't fit, you generate it. If we need a shot of a woman pouring coffee at 6am with golden hour lighting and the sourced clips look generic, you should be able to generate that in Higgsfield or Flow inside an hour and have it cut into the edit by end of day.



The editors who win in 2026 are the ones who can move fluidly between all three: cut creator UGC, source perfect supporting clips, and generate the impossible shots. That's what we're hiring for.



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



- Editing 5–15 ad variants per week across multiple brands

- Cutting hooks (we usually test 3–5 hook variants per concept, same body)

- Pacing edits for direct response — fast cuts, motion, pattern interrupts, captioned throughout

- Sourcing B-roll from stock libraries, social platforms, and free archives — and knowing what's legally clear to use

- Building reference boards fro
ta ad library, competitor ads, and viral organic content

- Generating A-roll talking-head clips when we need spokesperson angles we don't have footage for

- Creating AI B-roll: lifestyle shots, product close-ups, transformations, before/afters, environmental context

- Building character-consistent AI footage when we're running a series or recurring "spokesperson"

- Mixing UGC creator footage with sourced clips and AI-generated supplementary footage seamlessly

- Adding captions (burned-in, branded styling), sound design, music, SFX

- Versioning ads for different placements (Reels, Feed, Stories) and aspect ratios

- Communicating async via Slack/Loom with the media buyer on what's working and what's not



WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU



Editing chops:

- 2+ years editing DTC/UGC ads that actually ran on Meta or TikTok

- Portfolio with examples we can verify ran as paid ads (bonus if you have performance data)

- Native fluency in Premiere, CapCut, or DaVinci — we don't care which, just be fast

- Strong instinct for direct response: you know why a 0.8 second hook beats a 2 second one, you understand thumb-stop ratio, and you've watched enough Meta ad library to recognize patterns

- Caption and subtitle work that doesn't look like default CapCut

- Sound design that doesn't sound stock (royalty-free music is fine, lazy music choice is not)



B-roll sourcing skills:

- Active accounts or familiarity with Storyblocks, Artgrid, Envato, Motion Array, Pexels, Pixabay, or similar

- You know how to search efficiently — you don't burn 2 hours looking for the right clip

- You understand commercial licensing basics (what's safe, what's not, when in doubt how to verify)

- You have a system for saving and organizing reference inspiration (Pinterest boards, Notion, Eagle, Milanote — whatever works)

- You can pull fro
ta ad library and TikTok creative center to inform your edits and find inspiration footage



AI generation experience:

- Hands-on production experience with at least 2 of: Higgsfield (Soul, DoP, character training), Google Flow / Veo 3, Kling, Runway, Sora, Nano Banana

- You've solved real problems with these tools — character consistency across clips, lip sync, motion control, prompt engineering for specific aesthetics

- You understand the failure modes (warped hands, weird physics, identity drift) and how to work around them

- You have a perspective on which tool to reach for when — not just "I use whatever"



Process:

- Fast async communication

- Comfortable working from briefs, scripts, and reference ads

- Self-directed — we'll give you direction and references, but you should bring ideas

- Honest when something isn't working



BONUS POINTS



- Supplement, beauty, or health DTC experience

- You've reverse-engineered winning ads fro
ta ad library and can articulate why they work

- Familiarity with creative testing frameworks (hook-body-CTA structure, modular variants)

- You've used Higgsfield Soul for character consistency or trained custom characters

- ElevenLabs or similar AI voice work

- Motion graphics chops (After Effects, or template-based motion in CapCut)

- You follow people like Ed (Ad Burnouts), Barrett, Nick Shackelford, or have your own creative inspiration sources



LOGISTICS



- Type: Contract, with a clear path to ongoing retainer for the right person

- Hours: Start at ~15–25 hrs/week, can grow

- Location: Remote, async-friendly. Some overlap with PST hours preferred but not required

- Rate: Tell us yours. We pay competitively for editors who can actually do all three sides of this (UGC editing + B-roll sourcing + AI generation is rare — we know that)

- Tools we'll cover: AI generation tool subscriptions and stock library access if you don't already have them



HOW TO APPLY



Applications missing any of these get skipped:



1. Portfolio link — Vimeo, personal site, 
, Google Drive folder. We want to see DTC/UGC ads, not wedding videos or short films.



2. 2–3 AI-generated clips you've made — A-roll, B-roll, character work, whatever shows your range. Raw clips are fine. Tell us which tool and what the prompt/process was.



3. One ad you didn't make but love — link it and tell us in 3–4 sentences why it works. This tells us how you think.



4. Your B-roll sourcing stack — which stock libraries you have access to, where else you pull from, and your process for finding the right clip fast.



5. Your AI stack — which tools you use, which you'd reach for first, and one limitation of your favorite tool.



6. Your rate — hourly or per-edit, both fine. Be honest about where you are.



7. Availability — hours per week, time zone, when you can start.

title: Meta Ads Maker
description:
Job Title: Meta Ads Maker  (Hourly / Part-Time)



About the Brand

GOD MADE MAN® is a premium anti-aging skincare brand built specifically for Black men. We sell through our Shopify store at godmademan.store and run paid ads on Meta 
 and Instagram). 

We are a small, new brand with a clear identity and creative strategy. We can provide very specific, detailed creative direction for all our ad projects. We know exactly what we want — we need a skilled VA to actually put it all together. 

What This Role Is

This is a flexible hourly, part-time remote position with flexible hours. All ad strategy, copy, visual direction, prompts, and production briefs you need will be provided. Your job is to take that direction and execute it to a high standard, mostly using AI tools and video/image editing software and other typical resources.

This is a creative execution role — not a creative strategy role. Think of yourself as a skilled production assistant working from a highly detailed director's brief. However, we will appreciate your advice and input throughout the process.

Hours will be consistent week to week with room to grow as the brand scales.



Expected Hours

Starts at a minimum of 6-8 hours per week. Hours are flexible — you can work on your own schedule as long as deliverables are completed within agreed turnaround times. As output quality is confirmed and the brand grows, we will request more hours.



What You Will Do

Execute video ad productions: including avatar generation, lip-syncing, and B-roll assembly (using resources like HeyGen and Higgsfield AI–and/or your preferred tools).

Build and edit finished video ads: assembling talking head, UGC and various other types of footage, B-roll product shots, audio, and captions (using resources like CapCut or DaVinci Resolve–and/or your preferred tools)

Generate static image ads from provided reference images and copy, using resources like AdCreative.ai and Canva–and/or your preferred tools).

Generate product beauty shots and CGI-style visuals (using resources like Higgsfield Marketing Studio–and/or your preferred tools)

Produce voice conversions from provided reference audio files (using resources like ElevenLabs and Resemble AI–and/or your preferred tools). 

Upload and manage ad creatives in Meta Ads Manager — setting up campaigns, ad sets, and running A/B tests per provided instructions

Organize and maintain a clean library of all creative assets — video files, image files, audio files, and prompt documents.

Communicate clearly and proactively — flagging issues, confirming completion, and asking questions before starting work rather than after.



Tools* You Must Know — Required (*Note: We provide subscriptions, if needed.)

You must have demonstrable hands-on experience with all of these (or a VERY similar alternative instead):

HeyGen — avatar generation and lip-sync

CapCut or DaVinci Resolve — video assembly and editing

Canva — ad layout and design

Meta Ads Manager — campaign setup and creatives management

AdCreative.ai — static image ad generation

Tools You Should Know (or Be Able to Learn Quickly):

Higgsfield AI — Marketing Studio, Lipsync Studio, Soul 2.0, Cinema Studio

ElevenLabs — voice cloning and text-to-speech

Resemble AI — speech-to-speech voice conversion

CloudConvert and mp3cut.net — file conversion and audio editing utilities



Who You Are

Detail-oriented — you read briefs carefully and follow direction precisely before applying your own judgment

Proactive communicator — you ask clarifying questions upfront, not after delivering work that missed the mark

High standard for quality — you review your own output critically before submitting it

Comfortable with AI tools — you stay current with new features and can troubleshoot when a generation doesn't come out right.

Honest about your capabilities — if you don't know a tool, you say so rather than overpromising

Reliable — you meet deadlines, track your hours accurately, and communicate immediately if you have a problem, concern, complaint, or any “bad news” we should know about.



How Hours and Payment Work

You log your hours honestly using a time tracker — Time Doctor, Toggl, or Hubstaff are all acceptable

You submit a hours log at the end of each week with a brief summary of tasks completed

Payment is made weekly via PayPal, Wise, or GCash — whichever works best for you

Minimum commitment 6 hours per week.



What a Typical Week Looks Like

You will receive detailed written briefs for each ad — including the exact script, Higgsfield or HeyGen prompt, scene breakdown, B-roll timing, audio file, and reference images. Your job is to execute each brief completely and deliver a finished ad ready for Meta upload. You will also receive static ad briefs with reference images, copy, and product photos for AdCreative.ai and Canva execution. A typical week may involve 2–4 video ad productions and/or 2-4 static image ad variants.



Hourly Rate

$6–10/hour depending on skill level and portfolio quality. Rate reviewed upward after 30 days if output quality and reliability are confirmed. This is an ongoing engagement — not a one-time project. Consistent hours and a long-term working relationship are the goal.



Portfolio (REQUIRED)

Please include examples of Meta ad creative work you have produced — video and static image. Preference given to candidates with ecommerce, skincare, beauty, or men's grooming brand experience. Work produced using AI tools is preferred over traditional production work — we want to see that you know how to get quality output from the currently-available AI tools.



How to Apply

Please send the following:

A brief introduction — who you are, your background, and why this role fits your skills. (Important: Put the words “I read your job description” at the start of your introduction.)

Portfolio*: Links to or samples of at least 4 Meta video ads and 4 image ads that you have produced.

A list of the AI tools that you have solid, hands-on experience (please include ONLY tools you have actually used–not tools you only know about) 

Your time zone and the hours of the day that you typically work.

Your hourly rate expectation if different from the range listed above.

*Applications without a portfolio of samples cannot be considered.



One Last Thing

This brand has a very specific visual identity — premium, matte black and copper gold, built for Black men, authentic and non-generic. We are serious about quality. If your portfolio shows work that is polished, on-brand, and clearly executed with care — we really want to hear from you. If your work looks like AI defaults with no creative direction applied — this is not the right fit.

Our Promise: Providers LOVE working with us. We are ALWAYS kind and fair. We treat the people we work with very well.

title: Medical Insurance Billing Specialist
description:
About Us

We are a nonprofit organization dedicated to providing high-quality, accessible healthcare to vulnerable populations. Our Executive Director leads a mission-driven team, and we are seeking an experienced Medical Insurance Billing Specialist to provide high-level billing support. This role is essential in keeping our organization running smoothly, ensuring our patients receive timely care, and enabling our leadership to focus on strategic initiatives.



Position Overview

The Medical Insurance Billing Specialist will serve as a direct support to the Executive Director and medical providers. This role will be responsible for handling all billing processes. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, highly organized, proactive, and experienced in healthcare administration, Medicaid/insurance processes, and executive support.



Key Responsibilities



Medicaid and Insurance Billing: 

- Using the electronic medical record, submit all bills to insurances - specifically Medicaid on a weekly basis

- Review Explanation of Benefits and other insurance communications on a weekly basis, ensuring that all charges were paid for by the insurance company. 

- When claims were not paid by the insurance, examine the remark codes, fix claims, resubmit, or call Medicaid to figure out why the claim was not paid. 

- Track all claims not paid, to ensure they eventually do get paid. 

- Track ICD-10 and CPT code combinations that are not accepted, inform the providers of changes that need to be made in order to ensure smoother billing.



Other Tasks:

- Credentialing Communications - Handling all communications about provider insurance credentialing, interfacing with the credentialing company, and ensuring newly credentialed providers have EDI agreements established through the electronic medical record so that billing can take place.

- Patient Insurance Lookup - When needed, searching for Medicaid or insurance information on patients, inputting new insurance information into the electronic medical record, updating patient insurance information periodically, contacting insurance companies as needed to clarify.

title: : Underfloor Heating Estimator – Electric & Hydronic (Full-Time, Contract))
description:
About Comfort Heat

Comfort Heat is an established underfloor heating company based in Sydney, Australia, specialising in both electric and hydronic underfloor heating systems. We custom-design every project — from single bathrooms to whole-home systems — and pride ourselves on honest, expert advice and quality workmanship.

We already have a tea
mber in the Philippines and are looking to grow our Filipino team. Our director has personally visited the Philippines twice and had more than 10 Filipino tea
mbers in a previous business — so we understand remote work with Filipino professionals and genuinely value the relationship.



The Role

We're looking for a detail-oriented, tech-savvy Estimator to join our team full-time. You'll be preparing custom quotes and floor plan drawings for both electric and hydronic underfloor heating projects across Australia.

Every job we do is custom — based on the exact floor area and layout the customer wants heated. There are no cookie-cutter quotes here. You'll be working with real architectural plans, producing professional drawings, and preparing accurate quotes.

This is a role with real career progression. Once you've built your skills and product knowledge, you'll progress into a customer-facing role — communicating directly with clients via
 and phone to deliver quotes, answer questions, and build relationships.



What You'll Be Doing

• Receive architectural plans and drawings from customers (PDF/image format)

• Snip/copy the relevant floor plan and paste it into Microsoft Visio

• Resize and scale the drawing accurately to match real-world dimensions

• Add measurements to confirm the drawing is to scale

• Calculate floor areas that need heating based on the layout

• Select appropriate heating products based on a basic understanding of electric and hydronic systems (training provided)

• Prepare detailed quotes using our Excel templates — every quote is customised to the specific project

• Over time, learn to prepare heating layout drawings in Visio — showing the placement of electric heating cable or hydronic pipe runs over the floor plan

• Progress into client communication —
ing and calling clients to deliver quotes and manage enquiries once you're confident and experienced



What We're Looking For

Must-Haves:

* Strong Microsoft Excel skills (formulas, templates, formatting — you need to be confident here)

* Understand and interpret architectural floor plans (ideally some previously drawing or CAD experience)

* Tech-savvy — you pick up new software quickly and are comfortable working across multiple tools

* Ability to read and interpret architectural floor plans

* Excellent attention to detail — measurements and calculations need to be spot-on

* Strong English communication skills (written and verbal — you'll eventually be speaking with Australian clients)

* Self-starter mentality — you take ownership, work independently, and want to smash through your workload

* Own reliable computer, stable internet connection, and a quiet workspace

* Available to work Sydney, Australia business hours (AEST/AEDT)



Nice-to-Haves (but not required — we'll train the right person):

* Experience with Microsoft Visio or similar drafting/drawing software

* Background in construction, drafting, estimating, or engineering

* Experience with scaling drawings or working with architectural plans

* Basic understanding of underfloor heating, HVAC, or electrical/plumbing systems





Who You Are

• You're a self-starter who takes ownership and smashes through your work

• You're organised and can manage multiple quotes without dropping the ball

• You're curious and eager to learn — the heating industry might be new to you, but you're excited to understand it

• You're reliable — you show up on time, communicate proactively, and follow through

• You're ambitious — you want to grow into more responsibility, not just stay in a box



How to Apply

IMPORTANT: Start your application with the word "WARMTH" so we know you've read this entire ad.

Please include:

1. A brief introduction about yourself and why this role interests you

2. Your experience with Excel (specific examples, please)

3. Your experience with Visio or any drafting/drawing software (if applicable)

4. Your internet speed (screenshot is a bonus)

5. Your available start date

6. Your remuneration expectations 

Applications that don't follow these instructions will not be reviewed.
